Label.text: Panels in stacks of tabs and splits, the layout plain data that every move goes through. Drag a tab out of its strip and drop it into a stack, beside one, or along an edge; the preview stands where it would go, and a move the layout refuses says why. A torn tab dims in place meanwhile (the last button switches it to its strip closing up). With Shift held a tab floats instead, and a floating window dragged by its title docks whole wherever it is let go; with Shift it only moves.

Docking is the pointer's: drag a tab, with Shift to float it; close one by its cross or a middle click. The arrow at a strip's end lists its tabs, and dragged, carries the whole stack; the cross past it closes them all. From the keyboard, a focused tab's context menu (Shift+F10) is Move to and Close, and Ctrl+Shift+D picks a tab up. The last button puts the floats in OS windows of their own: a tab let go outside every window then floats there.
DockArea (GUI.Docking) over a DockController: a DockSpace for the main surface and a window for each float; splits are Splitters, stacks TabViews, the panels' contents kept as they move.
